article.name: GoodMemory
article.summary: GoodMemory is a TypeScript memory library whose scoped remember, recall, context assembly, correction, and deletion flows are backed by storage adapters. Bun defaults to durable SQLite, while Node without a configured durable adapter falls back to in-memory storage.

who_what.text: The official repository describes GoodMemory as a TypeScript memory layer for AI products and coding agents, with application, AI SDK, host, HTTP, and CLI integrations. Authentication and product authorization remain the integrating application's responsibility.

architecture.text: Typed records include facts, preferences, feedback, references, notes, episodes, profiles, and runtime continuity state. Records carry user scope and can include source method, extraction time, confidence, lifecycle, and temporal validity metadata.

Storage is abstracted behind document, session, and vector interfaces. The repository contains in-memory and SQLite implementations; the README also documents Postgres and injected adapters. Bun defaults to SQLite, while unsupported Node zero-config environments use memory storage.

The current recall path plans a query, retrieves candidates, applies bounded generalized selection when configured, assembles a result, and can attach evidence and trace data. Historical fitted selectors are documented as repository-only evaluation machinery rather than the production default.

behavior.text: remember composes extraction and write pipelines, applies redaction and persistence masking, coordinates document writes with rollback, then commits embeddings and optional claim projections. A result distinguishes committed, failed, and no-admissible-candidate outcomes.

The public README exposes feedback and targeted reviseMemory for correction. The revision service checks a scoped target and idempotency digest, conditionally writes a successor with the prior-target snapshot and evidence record, and can return a vector_write_failed warning after durable commit.

forget and deleteAllMemory are public operations. Admin deletion filters records against the requested scope and deletes scoped document records; omitted optional scope keys are wildcards. The deletion coordinator gates overlapping mutations and delete operations.

Recall defaults to rules-only unless the optional recommended preset is enabled. That preset can fuse BM25, entity adjacency, and available dense candidates with reciprocal-rank fusion; optional reranking and multi-hop add configured work. Selection budgets cap candidate and fact counts.

Recall evidence is linked to memory or archive IDs and filtered by complete scope. The evidence ledger can attach excerpts to claims and classify temporal status and relation; these are lineage annotations rather than independent truth adjudication.

Tracing is optional through a supplied sink. Spans represent operation status and HMAC-digested scope identifiers; retrieval traces can capture channels, scores, fallbacks, and reranker latency/status.

metrics.evidence: Recall and selection paths were inspected; no answer set was scored.
Scoped revision and lifecycle code were inspected; no correction probes were run.
Scope deletion and forget paths were inspected; no post-delete probes were run.
Five-part scope encoding and scope-aware evidence selection were inspected; no cross-scope workload was run.
Source/evidence links and ledger classifications were inspected; no response claims were adjudicated.
Bounded retrieval and trace fields exist; no runtime timings were collected.
Provider-dependent paths are documented; no token usage or charges were measured.
SQLite and adapter paths were inspected; no corpus-attributable byte count was collected.

limits.text: This review is pinned source inspection, not an operational, security, or quality audit. It cannot establish end-to-end correctness, provider availability, hostile-caller isolation, deletion from backups or external stores, measured quality, or resource use.

Durability depends on storage selection: Bun defaults to local SQLite while Node without a durable adapter falls back to in-memory. Rules-only recall is the default; dense retrieval and provider reranking require configuration.

The scope model and evidence annotations demonstrate intended boundaries, but this review did not test whether each adapter and host integration enforces them identically. The integrating application owns authentication and product authorization.

benchmark.note: No GoodMemory runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run in this review. Source observations and upstream documentation statements are not measured results.
